South Africa's bowling response was spearheaded by Kagiso Rabada (4/91), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. scorecards.inningsCommentary: South Africa embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 380 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 83 from HM Amla, complemented by a commanding 123-run stand between HM Amla and Francois Plessis that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.21 RPO. England's bowling response was spearheaded by Moeen Ali (5/69), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 202/10 (62.5 ov), South Africa succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as England's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Old Trafford commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 362/10 (108.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, South Africa countered with 226/10 (72.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 7 Wickets for 39 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Moeen Ali delivered a masterclass for England (89 Runs & 7 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (England 51%) and allowing England to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, South Africa faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. England's bowling unit, bolstered by James Anderson (6 Runs & 7 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing England won by 177 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: England's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While South Africa produced fighting phases, England won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
